tasks.short: Assess proposed project changes, agree trade-offs, approve changes, and update the project baseline.

steps.what: Collect the change request, current baseline, costs, and delivery status.
Calculate schedule, budget, and resource impacts for alternative changes.
Draft the change proposal and explain assumptions and trade-offs.

loop.input: Change request, calculated scenarios, and cited baseline sections.
loop.output: Draft change proposal with assumptions, alternatives, and source references.
loop.check: Check figures against scenario outputs; require sources for factual claims and flag missing assumptions.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair within a fixed token budget; unresolved gaps return to the project manager.
loop.why_not_simpler: Calculations are deterministic, but explaining project-specific trade-offs requires reading and writing free text.

steps.what: Discuss feasibility, competing priorities, and commitments with affected leads.
Approve, reject, or defer the recommended baseline change.
Update the baseline and change log from the recorded decision.

tasks.design: An integration assembles versioned evidence from the {PROJECT}, {ERP}, and {DOCS}; deterministic calculations produce comparable change scenarios. A bounded drafting loop prepares the proposal, people negotiate commitments, and approval in the {PROJECT} triggers only the authorised baseline changes.
tasks.previous_blocker: Cost, dependency, and resource records sit in different systems. Scenario assumptions and approval limits often remain implicit.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding reduces the effort of building connectors, scenario calculators, and document templates. Existing approval features can enforce the final decision.
tasks.still_hard: Dependencies can be incomplete, resource promises can change, and commercial consequences require judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising unrealistic commitments, negotiating trade-offs, and accepting responsibility for the chosen change.

ambition.what: Early scope trade-off reviews before a milestone becomes unrecoverable

tasks.altitude: The project manager spends less time assembling proposals and more time testing delivery options with leads. Sponsor approval rights remain unchanged; delegated change limits require an explicit governance decision.

reach.task: Compare process-change alternatives using sensitivity analysis.
reach.learn: Scenario modelling, explicit assumptions, and benefits measurement.

evidence.claim: Versioned change records, dependency calculations, and approval-triggered updates can use deterministic software.
The digest provides no direct case demonstrating automated project-change approval.

assumptions: The typical baseline is in the {PROJECT}, with supporting documents in the {DOCS} and scenario work in the {SPREADSHEET}.
Resource inputs describe availability and commitments; the solution does not score individual worker performance.
Time shares and remaining effort are planning estimates informed by the supplied priors.
Build ranges cover a pilot and working effort for access and consultation; elapsed approval waits may be longer.
unknowns: Which baseline fields and dependencies are maintained reliably.
Who may approve changes at each cost and schedule threshold.
Whether the {PROJECT} supports versioned updates and approval hooks.
Which national rules require employee consultation for the proposed data use.
research_questions: Which native scenario and approval features can replace custom development?
How should simultaneous baseline changes be detected and blocked?
new_work: Review draft assumptions and unsupported claims.
Resolve missing dependencies and stale resource commitments.
Maintain approval thresholds, field mappings, and baseline version checks.
Investigate failed or partially applied updates.

tasks.short: Define supplier needs, compare vendors or consultants, assess fit, and secure an approved selection.

steps.what: Agree project requirements, selection criteria, and spending limits.
Review supplier records and capability documents to form a shortlist.

loop.input: Approved supplier records and capability documents matched to explicit requirements.
loop.output: Candidate shortlist with cited capability evidence and missing information.
loop.check: Apply eligibility rules deterministically; verify cited passages and review exclusions.
loop.stop: One extraction per document and one repair within document and token limits; uncertain cases go to procurement.
loop.why_not_simpler: Eligibility fields support filters, but capability evidence often appears only in free-text documents.

steps.what: Send standard requests for proposals to shortlisted suppliers.
Compare received proposals, prices, exclusions, and delivery commitments.

loop.input: Supplier proposals and the approved comparison schema.
loop.output: Evidence-linked comparison with prices, exclusions, commitments, and gaps.
loop.check: Recalculate totals deterministically; verify currencies, tax treatment, units, and source passages.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair per proposal within a fixed token budget; unresolved fields remain blank.
loop.why_not_simpler: Proposals use different layouts and prose for scope exclusions and delivery commitments.

steps.what: Test supplier fit through clarification calls, references, and commercial discussions.
Approve the preferred supplier and commercial limits.
Send the approved selection notice with its contractual conditions.
File the evaluation and open the contracting handoff.

tasks.design: The {PROCUREMENT} holds requirements, eligibility rules, supplier records, and approval limits; bounded extraction loops turn capability documents and proposals from the {DOCS} into cited comparisons. People assess fit and negotiate, while configured workflows gate external requests and notices and pass the approved selection to the {CLM}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Supplier evidence arrives in inconsistent documents and mail threads. Evaluation criteria and approval records are often scattered.
tasks.enabler_now: Bounded document extraction can populate a fixed comparison schema. AI-assisted coding makes validation and document connectors cheaper to build.
tasks.still_hard: References can be selective, delivery capability is uncertain, and attractive proposals can conceal commercial dependencies.
tasks.human_edge: Testing credibility, understanding team fit, negotiating commitments, and defending a fair selection.

ambition.what: Evidence-based consideration of smaller suppliers outside the incumbent shortlist

tasks.altitude: The project manager spends more time testing supplier capability and less time copying proposal details. Selection and spending rights remain with their current holders.

reach.task: Assess supplier concentration and continuity exposure.
reach.learn: Supplier dependency mapping, financial resilience signals, and contingency options.

evidence.claim: Pactum's SUEZ case documents procurement requisition review automation; it does not establish autonomous project supplier selection.
Fixed comparison schemas, arithmetic checks, and approval routing can be deterministic; qualitative supplier fit still requires judgement.

assumptions: A procurement specialist supports project sourcing, with proposals commonly arriving through the {EMAIL}.
The solution compares suppliers and does not evaluate individuals for employment.
Selection notices use approved wording and do not bypass contracting authority.
GDPR applies to personal contact and reference data; employment-related consultant evaluation requires separate EU AI Act assessment.
Time shares and remaining effort are estimates; build ranges cover a pilot rather than every supplier category.
Access and consultation ranges represent working effort; national requirements and elapsed waits vary.
unknowns: Whether consultant selection includes recruitment or worker evaluation.
Which supplier sources may be searched and retained.
How conflicts of interest, eligibility, and spending limits are recorded.
Whether existing supplier records cover smaller or new suppliers adequately.
research_questions: Which native sourcing features support evidence-linked comparisons and approval routing?
How reliably can extraction distinguish fixed fees, estimates, exclusions, and optional work?
new_work: Verify extracted exclusions and commercial qualifications.
Review shortlist omissions and incomplete supplier evidence.
Maintain comparison schemas, eligibility rules, and notice templates.
Monitor access permissions and retention of supplier contact and reference data.

tasks.short: Arrange project meetings, prepare decisions, facilitate discussion, and record agreed actions.

steps.what: Decide the meeting purpose, required decisions, and participants.
Chase participant availability through messages.
Book the meeting and issue calendar invitations.
Prepare the agenda, decision questions, and supporting material.

loop.input: Meeting brief, open issues, decision requests, and linked project records.
loop.output: Draft agenda with decision questions, owners, and source links.
loop.check: Require valid record links; distinguish requested decisions from agreed decisions and flag missing owners.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair within a fixed token budget; the project manager completes unresolved items.
loop.why_not_simpler: Issue descriptions need concise synthesis into useful discussion and decision questions.

steps.what: Facilitate discussion, resolve disagreement, and confirm decisions and commitments.
Write draft minutes from the meeting notes.

loop.output: Draft minutes separating decisions, open questions, and proposed actions.
loop.check: Link decisions to explicit notes; never infer agreement, an owner, or a due date.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair within a fixed token budget; ambiguous commitments remain questions.
loop.why_not_simpler: Informal notes need language interpretation to produce readable minutes without inventing agreement.

steps.what: Confirm the minutes and circulate the approved record.
Enter agreed actions, owners, and due dates into the project tracker.

tasks.design: Configured availability rules in the {CALENDAR} replace availability chasing and book routine internal meetings. Bounded loops prepare agendas and minutes from the {PROJECT} and written notes in the {DOCS}; the project manager facilitates discussion and approves the record before agreed actions enter the {PROJECT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Availability chasing, meeting preparation, and action entry were separate routines. Informal notes did not provide reliable structured inputs.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing calendar configuration handles routine booking. Bounded drafting and structured action fields connect the surrounding paperwork at modest build cost.
tasks.still_hard: Conflicting priorities, power differences, and unclear commitments require active human facilitation.
tasks.human_edge: Getting the right people to speak, noticing unresolved disagreement, and securing explicit commitments.

ambition.what: An asynchronous decision queue for contributors who cannot attend project meetings

tasks.altitude: The project manager spends less time arranging meetings and more time resolving disagreement. Decision rights remain with the existing participants and sponsors.

reach.task: Coordinate decision agendas across senior stakeholders.
reach.learn: Agenda prioritisation, escalation etiquette, and calendar constraints.

evidence.claim: Availability rules, calendar invitations, approval routing, and action creation can use existing configuration.
The digest provides no direct meeting-facilitation automation case; the design preserves human facilitation.

assumptions: Routine meetings are internal and participants expose usable free/busy information through the {CALENDAR}.
Booking follows agreed working hours, required attendance, and rescheduling limits.
Written facilitator notes are used; recording and employee monitoring are outside the design.
Confirmed actions are stored as structured fields alongside approved minutes.
Time shares preserve substantial human meeting time despite the administrative automation opportunity.
Build ranges cover a pilot; national consultation requirements and access approval waits vary.
unknowns: Whether free/busy access covers all required participants.
Which meetings include external participants or confidential topics.
Who may publish minutes and confirm disputed commitments.
Whether national rules require consultation for the proposed note-processing arrangement.
research_questions: Which native booking features satisfy mandatory-attendee and working-hour constraints?
How should action updates avoid duplicates when approved minutes are corrected?
new_work: Review agenda priorities and ambiguous draft minutes.
Handle calendar conflicts that cannot satisfy booking rules.
Maintain participant permissions and document retention settings.
Resolve disputed commitments and correct linked project actions.

tasks.short: Assemble project costs and progress, estimate remaining work, and submit checked budget and status reports.

steps.what: Collect actual costs, commitments, delivery status, and approved budget figures.
Reconcile project codes, reporting periods, commitments, and missing costs.
Estimate remaining work and explain forecast assumptions with delivery leads.
Compile budget estimates, cost tables, progress measures, and explanatory commentary.
Check report totals, assumptions, completeness, and recipient-specific disclosures.
Approve release and submit the report to authorised recipients.

tasks.design: Scheduled integrations load the {ERP}, {PROCUREMENT}, and {PROJECT} into the {DATA_PLATFORM}, where rules reconcile periods, codes, and commitments and expose exceptions in the {BI}. Structured forecasts and approved commentary populate report templates in the {DOCS}; a release approval controls distribution through the {EMAIL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Project codes and accounting periods do not align cleanly across systems. Forecast commentary and remaining-work estimates are collected separately.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding makes mappings, reconciliation rules, and report templates faster to build. The calculations and document assembly need no model loop.
tasks.still_hard: Late invoices, uncertain completion estimates, and disputed progress measures still need investigation and discussion.
tasks.human_edge: Challenging optimistic estimates, recognising hidden delivery risk, and explaining uncertainty to sponsors or customers.

ambition.what: Weekly forecast-to-complete reviews for projects approaching budget limits

tasks.altitude: The project manager spends less time compiling reports and more time challenging forecasts with delivery leads. Report preparation grants no additional budget or spending authority.

reach.task: Compare project forecasts and identify recurring sources of overruns.
reach.learn: Variance analysis, forecast calibration, and separating timing differences from structural cost changes.

evidence.claim: Project cost reconciliation, variance calculations, and template-based reporting are suitable for deterministic software.
Reporting automation does not establish the reliability of estimates to complete; those depend on delivery evidence and judgement.

assumptions: The {ERP} holds accounting actuals, the {PROCUREMENT} holds commitments, and the {PROJECT} holds delivery status.
The {SPREADSHEET} currently ties these records together before report assembly in the {DOCS}.
Variance drivers and commentary can be captured as structured fields and approved text.
The project manager may release routine reports; budget changes follow a separate approval process.
Aggregate project costs are sufficient; individual performance scoring is outside the design.
Time shares and remaining effort are estimates; build ranges cover a pilot and consultation effort, excluding uncertain calendar waits.
unknowns: Which project codes join actuals, commitments, and delivery records reliably.
How accruals, tax, currencies, and internal labour costs must be treated.
Which reports go to customers and require additional approval.
Whether source systems provide timely exports or supported interfaces.
Which national consultation requirements apply to access to employee-related cost data.
research_questions: Which native project-accounting reports already cover the required figures?
Which reconciliation controls best detect double-counted commitments and late postings?
new_work: Resolve unmatched costs, stale commitments, and reporting-period exceptions.
Maintain code mappings, calculation rules, templates, and recipient permissions.
Review forecast assumptions and investigate repeated forecast bias.
Monitor source freshness and failed report deliveries.

role.altitude: The project manager's week shifts from gathering records and producing paperwork toward testing delivery assumptions, resolving dependencies, and negotiating commitments. Existing sponsor, budget-owner, and procurement decision rights remain in place unless explicitly delegated.
reach: Management analyst: compare project outcomes and forecast reliability.
Supply chain manager: assess supplier dependency and continuity exposure.
Executive administrative assistant: coordinate decision agendas across senior stakeholders.
skills_to_grow: Supplier evidence assessment and commercial judgement.
Facilitation, negotiation, and explicit commitment setting.
Data permissions, exception management, and automation acceptance checks.
role.ambitious_version: Provide a cross-project decision service that combines current cost, dependency, and supplier evidence into comparable options for sponsors. The service recommends where intervention matters; accountable people approve commitments and changes.
